Overview

The Assassin is a dagger burst class that lives on buffs. Hits engrave Insignias on the target, Insignia Explosion cashes them in, and Heart Gore fires on crits and resets itself on the next crit. The biggest damage bonus comes from hitting the target in the back, so positioning matters more than on any other class.

The build in one sentence

Stay behind the boss, weave Quick Slice all the time, press Insignia Explosion the moment it is ready and Heart Gore on every crit — and put everything you have into the 20 seconds of Illusive Clone, when Heart Gore has no cooldown at all.

What to expect in Season 1

  • Burst, then a gap. On KR/TW the level-25 tier of Illusive Clone lets good players keep it up permanently. Global stops at 20: about 20 seconds of burst on a 1 min 30 s cooldown, and between windows you play fillers while Heart Gore depends on crit luck.
  • The buffs don't line up. Swift Contract and Savage Fang come back in a minute, Illusive Clone in a minute and a half — you keep deciding whether to wait or to press.
  • Back uptime is damage. On a dummy it is 100%; in a real fight expect 60–80%, and every hit from the front loses the Rear Smite bonus.
  • Fragile. No block, little defense — mistakes that a Gladiator survives kill you.

Arthars' verdict: a fun, high-skill class that needs several times more work than a Gladiator or a Sorcerer for the same damage or less. Pick it because you like the playstyle, not for the numbers.

The PvE mode follows Arthars Gaming's Assassin video for the global launch (September 30, recorded on the Taiwan server), read frame by frame; the video has no captions, so its text was taken from the audio by speech recognition and every name and number checked against the screen. XifanGG's PvE guide (October 9, also played on the Taiwan server, over 1 million combat power) adds the burst order, a second hotbar and macro setup, and the alternatives marked with his name.

Patch Season 1. The build is checked against guides from the global servers: 4 stigmas, cap 20.

Overview

In PvP the Assassin is a chain of crowd control: get behind the target, stun it, and keep it stunned or knocked down while Illusive Clone turns every hit into a burst. Most of the damage lands from behind — a fight you take from the front is a fight you lose.

The build in one sentence

Stealth in, Shadowstrike behind the target for the stun, Shadow Fall on the stunned target for the knockdown, and burst with Illusive Clone and the macro inside that window; Shadowstep is your way out.

This mode follows AlanStriker's PvP setup (English, global, October 9 — 100k Combat Power, skills at 12–16): skill picks, stigmas, his hotbar and macro, read from the video frames. Keyba's PvP build (English, global, October 8 — duels and small groups) adds the stigma alternatives and the passive order. Arena, Battlefield and the Abyss are the PvP content in Season 1.

Patch Season 1. The build is checked against guides from the global servers: 4 stigmas, cap 20.

Passives for PvP (Keyba): Apply Poison first — a 15% chance to cut the target's healing by 40% — then Rear Smite and Exploit Weakness. AlanStriker adds points to Revitalization Contract: about 45% HP back when you drop to 10%.

Passives

Skill points max almost all passives while you level. Gear lines are the scarce part: the class wants four passives there and only two or three fit.

PassivePriority on gearWhy
Rear Smite1Back attack and PvE damage boost — the strongest passive; it gives damage even from the front.
Exploit Weakness2Critical Hit and an Attack buff that is up almost all the time in combat; Illusive Clone multiplies it.
Assault Stance2Critical Damage Boost; Swift Contract multiplies it.
Determination3Extra damage on a low-HP target — aLuckyRO counts it among the most important: every boss spends the end of the fight there.
Impact Hit4Double Chance — only 3.3% at level 10, next to nothing in PvE (aLuckyRO). Keep it for PvP; on PvE gear take Determination first (XifanGG keeps Impact Hit as his fourth).
Ambush Stance, Heightened Sixth Sensepoints onlyMaxed by skill points; not worth a gear line.
Revitalization Contractpoints onlyRestores a big part of your HP once you drop to 10% (46% on XifanGG's character) — a safety net on a hard boss.
Apply Poison, Defense BreakskipPoison is under 1% of your damage; Defense Break is a PvP passive.

Gear & stats

  • Rings: the only place for active skills — Heart Gore, Quick Slice, Insignia Explosion, Ambush. They take the key skills from 14 to 16.
  • Weapon and guard: never put skills there — their damage lines are worth more than one skill level.
  • Other pieces: Rear Smite first; any of the next three passives is fine. Don't chase a perfect set in Season 1 — global gear has one line less and also rolls Might, Precision and Combat Speed there.
  • Critical Hit matters more than on other classes: Heart Gore resets only on a crit.
  • Wings: Talisra Wings give 4% Cooldown Reduction — the best wings for the class (XifanGG). They are in the Season shop → Special, for season points: save them for these.
  • Manastones: Attack, Critical Hit, Accuracy.

Titles — which one to equip in each slot: After level 45 → Titles. Pets and Genus Insight — what to level and what to roll at 10: Pets → Genus Insight.

Gear & stats

  • Gear as in PvE — a separate PvP set is nice to have, but not worth giving up your PvE gear for (Keyba).
  • Theostone: Courage — a 1% chance to deal 10,000 damage, enough to finish a stunned target (Keyba).
  • Azphel, the level-45 Daevanion board, is all PvP stats. AlanStriker buys extra points for the PvP board, and his Combat Power is higher in the PvP setup because of it.

Arcana

Season 1 has five cards and two sets. The Assassin is the one class that must take Illusion (cooldowns) on the Mirror, which makes four Primal Vigor cards the natural set.

CardStatSetRoll for
ChaliceTime (Combat Speed)Primal VigorWhichever of the three key skills is still short of 20
ParchmentLifePrimal VigorQuick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion — all three
CompassFreedom (Accuracy)Primal VigorStorm Rampage, Ambush, Savage Roar — to reach 16
MirrorIllusion (cooldowns)Primal VigorRear Smite, Exploit Weakness; Impact Hit
BellDestruction (Attack)Magic ArmorAssault Stance

The Parchment is the grind. All three skills you want at 20 sit on this one card, and a Season 1 card lets you choose only two of its four lines. Leveling the card adds four random +1s — hope for an even spread (+2 on each) rather than +4 on one: the Chalice can then add the missing +2. If it doesn't work out, keep Heart Gore and Insignia Explosion at 20 and leave Quick Slice at 16.

The Compass and the Bell are relaxed: nothing on them has to reach 20. All these cards are replaced when Season 2 brings new ones.

Daevanion boards

Daevanion takes your skills from 10 to 14 and adds stats. Each blue node gives +1 level to its skill.

  • Priority: head for the orange corner nodes — Combat Speed and Cooldown Reduction on Nezekan, Damage Boost on Zikel — and take the path that passes the blue nodes of Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Quick Slice and the green ones of your key passives such as Exploit Weakness (XifanGG); Ambush and Storm Rampage after that.
  • Critical Damage early: for an Assassin the Vaizel orange Critical Damage Boost pays off from the start — it crits from day one, unlike most classes (aLuckyRO).
  • Priority: the same orange corner nodes as in PvE (Combat Speed, cooldowns, Damage Boost and Tolerance, Critical Damage), and the blue nodes that take Shadow Fall and Whirlwind Slice to 12 for their stun and knockdown picks (AlanStriker, Keyba).
  • Ariel (new, October 21): a sixth board, for PvE. Its points don't come from levels: Ariel Fragments drop in the Hard mode of Krao Cave and Draupnir (item level 2600), and 100 fragments become one Daevanion Crystal: Ariel in Substance Morph (Special → Daevanion) — up to 30 crystals from each dungeon, so 60 points per character. Its route is on the Ariel tab of the board below. Azphel stays PvP-only.
  • Azphel (level 45) is all PvP Damage Boost and Tolerance — take it, and Triniel earlier.

Stigmas

All four slots are buffs. Level Illusive Clone to 20 first — it eats most of your stigma shards — then the rest.

XifanGG's order is different: Swift Contract to 10 and Illusive Clone to 15 first, then Swift Contract to 20 before Illusive Clone — its last tier adds 10% Combat Speed, and Combat Speed is what the class needs most. Both work; his order gives steadier damage while shards are short.

  • No permanent Illusive Clone. The tier that shortens its cooldown on back crits is level 25 — not in global.
  • Illusive Clone Lv 20
    Your burst: for 20 seconds at level 20 (17 at 15) Heart Gore has no cooldown and you deal 20% extra damage, with +20% Critical Damage and ×1.5 Exploit Weakness on top. Cooldown 1 min 30 s. Most of your damage happens inside it — use it on the boss, never on trash. aLuckyRO: essential until Heart Gore reaches 16; with enough crits Heart Gore resets by itself and the slot can be swapped for a while, but at 20 it comes back for its damage boost.

    • 10+20% Critical Damage Boost for the duration
    • 15x1.5 [Exploit Weakness] effect for the duration
    • 2050% chance to deal extra damage on Critical Hit for the duration
    All specializations
    • 5+10% Status Effect Chance for the duration
    • 10+20% Critical Damage Boost for the duration
    • 15x1.5 [Exploit Weakness] effect for the duration
    • 2050% chance to deal extra damage on Critical Hit for the duration
  • Swift Contract Lv 15 20
    +20% Combat Speed, and ×1.5 Rear Smite and Assault Stance for the duration. 15 is enough to start; 20 adds 10% more Combat Speed.

Macro & rotation

?The macro key is not bound by default: bind it in Settings → Key Settings → General → Macro. Use the mouse button the guide names — usually RMB, held together with the basic attack on LMB.

AION 2 has two separate tools:

  • Hotbar line — several skills stacked on one hotbar button. Pressing it casts the highest-priority skill that's ready, and in AION 2 the bottom slot has the highest priority. The cards show each line top to bottom as in the game.
  • In-game macro — while you hold its key, it presses your hotbar buttons in order and cancels animation tails. Skills on cooldown are skipped.

1. Hotbar lines

EDamage line
  1. 4 Savage Roar
  2. 3 Ambush
  3. 2 Heart Gore
  4. 1 Insignia Explosion

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

Insignia Explosion fires every time it is ready, Heart Gore on every crit. When neither is available the line falls to the fillers: Ambush first, Savage Roar last.

7Buff line
  1. 4 Triniel's Dagger
  2. 3 Savage Fang
  3. 2 Swift Contract
  4. 1 Illusive Clone

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

Arthars keeps all four stigmas on one button and presses it by hand — never from the macro, or the buffs go off out of sync.

2. In-game macro

One step — the damage line, 10 ms — on a key you can hold all the time. Quick Slice stays out of the macro: hold its key together with the macro key, and the game weaves it in between the line's skills.

  1. 1Damage line10 ms

Arthars' video shows the hotbar but not the macro window; the macro is the one from XifanGG's macro window (October 9): only the Insignia line, Quick Slice held alongside it.

3. What you actually press

  • HoldThe macro key together with Quick Slice — every Quick Slice hit shortens Insignia Explosion.
  • BurstIllusive Clone + Swift Contract, Shadowstrike for its +20% Critical Damage, Savage Fang, then Triniel's Dagger straight away to cut the cooldowns (XifanGG's order). For the next 20 seconds it is Heart Gore after Heart Gore — use Flash Slice to stay behind the boss.
  • Between windowsSwift Contract and Savage Fang come back before Illusive Clone. Either hold them for the next Clone (bigger burst) or use them on cooldown (steadier damage) — there is no agreed answer; on short fights hold them.
  • StaggerStorm Rampage on a staggered boss, weaving Quick Slice — it pulls every cooldown down by seconds.
  • PositionShadowstrike, Flash Slice and Infiltrate all put you behind the target. Use them to stay there, not as damage buttons.

Where the damage comes from in Arthars' test on a dummy: Heart Gore about 30%, Insignia Explosion about 25%, everything else 6% or less each.

4. Another setup: XifanGG

Fewer skills in the macro, more by hand: the in-game macro holds only the Insignia line, and a mouse macro presses it together with Quick Slice.

  • Insignia line (5): Insignia Explosion, then Storm Rampage — it only fires on a staggered boss — then Heart Gore. New players can put Savage Roar on top as a filler.
  • Buffs (2): Illusive Clone and Swift Contract on one key — you still see both cooldowns, so you don't miss the burst window.
  • Dashes (Q): Infiltrate, Shadow Fall and Whirlwind Slice on one key — all of them take you to the boss or behind it. Infiltrate fires after a dodge (Shift).
  • In-game macro: one step — the Insignia line, 10 ms. Bind it to a key in Settings → Key settings → General → Macro.
  • Mouse macro: in his mouse software one button presses Quick Slice and the in-game macro key together and repeats while held — he binds Quick Slice to a second key for this (Settings → Key settings → Quickslot). Turn on Skill Queue in Settings → Combat → Controls, or the two don't mix well.

Read from XifanGG's skill window (7:12) and macro settings (8:00–9:30). He doesn't show which mouse buttons his side keys are — copy the lines, not the keys.

AlanStriker's PvP bar (video of October 9, frames 15:27–15:30): the stuns and dashes on their own keys, one line for the damage skills, and a five-step macro that opens with Illusive Clone.

TAmbush line
  1. 4 Savage Roar
  2. 3 Heart Gore
  3. 2 Insignia Explosion

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

Ambush first — it breaks shields — then Insignia Explosion, Heart Gore and Savage Roar as they come up.

QShadowstrike line
  1. 2 Infiltrate
  2. 1 Shadowstrike

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

Infiltrate sits on top of Shadowstrike: the same key gives a second dash while Shadowstrike is on cooldown (AlanStriker says so at 9:55; the frame hides that part of the bar).

  1. 1Illusive Clone5 · 10 ms
  2. 2Quick SliceLMB · 10 ms
  3. 3Ambush lineT · 10 ms
  4. 4Whirlwind Slice4 · 10 ms

  • OpenShadow Walk for stealth, get close, then Shadowstrike on Q behind the target — stun.
  • BurstHold the macro: Illusive Clone and the damage line fire inside the stun. Shadow Fall on E as soon as the target is stunned — the knockdown keeps the window open.
  • ChainEvery stun from Insignia Explosion, Whirlwind Slice or Aerial Bind is another Shadow Fall. Shields go down to Ambush.
  • OutShadowstep on 1 when you are low or the enemy bursts: back, stealth, then dash in again with Flash Slice on 3 or Shadowstrike on Q.

AlanStriker's variant: take Quick Slice out of the macro and hold the left mouse button and the macro together — Quick Slice fires more often and brings Insignia Explosion back faster.

Recap

  • Skills: Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Quick Slice 16 → 20; Ambush and Storm Rampage 16; the rest 12, Shadowstrike 8.
  • Stigmas: Illusive Clone 20, Swift Contract 15 → 20, Savage Fang 15, Triniel's Dagger 10.
  • Passives on gear: Rear Smite, then Exploit Weakness, Assault Stance, Determination.
  • Play: stay behind the boss, burst inside Illusive Clone, Triniel's Dagger right after the buffs.

Recap

  • Skills: Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Savage Roar, Ambush 16; Shadowstrike, Shadow Fall, Whirlwind Slice, Flash Slice, Infiltrate 12 with their stun, range and shield picks.
  • Stigmas: Illusive Clone 15, Aerial Bind, Shadowstep, Shadow Walk (Smoke Bomb in duels); Keyba: Spiral Slice and Triniel's Dagger instead of the stealth pair.
  • Passives: Apply Poison, Rear Smite, Exploit Weakness.
  • Play: stealth, Shadowstrike from behind, Shadow Fall on the stun, burst inside Illusive Clone, Shadowstep out.

How to fight while leveling

  • Packs: Savage Fang (5 Insignias) → Insignia Explosion → Whirlwind Slice; Throw Shadowblade resets on a kill for the next pull.
  • Elites: get behind → Ambush → Savage Roar to stack Insignias → Insignia Explosion → Heart Gore on crits.
  • Mana: Quick Slice restores MP — keep it on LMB.
  • Low HP: Shadow Fall absorbs HP; Defiance heals when you're stuck.

Leveling macro

?The macro key is not bound by default: bind it in Settings → Key Settings → General → Macro. Use the mouse button the guide names — usually RMB, held together with the basic attack on LMB.

While leveling, before Heart Gore reaches 16, a simpler setup works from level 1: the Insignia line in the in-game macro on the middle mouse button, Quick Slice on LMB and Heart Gore on Q. For farming mobs use Throw Shadowblade (2) and RMB. Early build at 1–45: Quick Slice, Savage Roar, Insignia Explosion and Heart Gore to 12, everything else to 8.
